items.title: A client with suspected DVT should not have the affected leg ___. The nurse should assess for pulmonary embolism symptoms such as sudden ___ and chest pain.
items.content: massaged|dyspnea
items.rationale: Massage is avoided because of embolization concern. Sudden dyspnea and chest pain may indicate PE and require emergency evaluation.

items.title: A client is found unresponsive with RR 5/min, pinpoint pupils, and suspected opioid exposure. Select the condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:opioid overdose with respiratory depression|actions:provide airway and ventilatory support;administer naloxone and repeat per protocol if needed|monitor:respiratory rate and oxygenation;level of consciousness and recurrent sedation
items.rationale: Ventilation is the immediate priority. Naloxone reverses opioid effects but may wear off before the opioid, so monitor for recurrence.

items.title: Highlight findings suggesting acute kidney injury: rising creatinine;reduced urine output;new hyperkalemia;stable baseline creatinine;new fluid overload.
items.content: segments:rising creatinine|reduced urine output|new hyperkalemia|stable baseline creatinine|new fluid overload|correct:1,2,3,5
items.rationale: Rising creatinine, oliguria, hyperkalemia, and fluid overload are complications or indicators of acute kidney injury.

items.title: A client is prescribed 1.2 g of an antibiotic. The vial concentration after reconstitution is 400 mg/mL. How many mL are needed?
A client's lactate decreases from 5.2 to 4.7 to 4.5 mmol/L after initial treatment but remains elevated. What is the best interpretation?
items.content: Perfusion may be improving slowly but remains abnormal; continue reassessment and prescribed sepsis management.
items.rationale: A downward trend is encouraging, but persistent elevation may indicate ongoing hypoperfusion or other causes and needs continued evaluation.

items.title: A client with a tibial fracture in a cast reports escalating pain despite medication. The calf is tense, pain increases with passive stretch, and sensation is tingling. What should the nurse do?
items.content: Notify the orthopedic surgeon immediately, perform and document neurovascular checks, keep the limb at heart level, and prepare for urgent cast release or fasciotomy as directed.
items.rationale: Pain out of proportion, passive-stretch pain, tense swelling, and paresthesia suggest compartment syndrome. Delay can cause irreversible muscle and nerve injury.

items.title: A client with pneumonia is confused, febrile, and hypotensive. BP is 82/46 mm Hg, lactate is 4.3 mmol/L, and oxygen saturation is 91%. Which action should the nurse prioritize while the sepsis response is activated?
items.content: Establish large-bore IV access and begin the prescribed isotonic crystalloid bolus, reassessing perfusion frequently.
items.rationale: Hypotension with elevated lactate indicates impaired tissue perfusion. Prompt isotonic fluid resuscitation is a priority unless contraindicated; reassess response and prepare for vasopressors if hypotension persists.

items.title: A conscious client with diabetes reports tremors and diaphoresis. Capillary glucose is 54 mg/dL. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Give 15 g of rapid-acting oral carbohydrate; recheck glucose in 15 minutes; repeat treatment if glucose remains below 70 mg/dL; provide a snack or meal when glucose recovers if the next meal is not imminent.
items.rationale: A conscious client who can swallow safely should receive rapid carbohydrate, followed by a 15-minute recheck and repeat treatment if needed. Severe altered consciousness or inability to swallow requires glucagon or IV dextrose rather than oral intake.

items.title: A client receiving magnesium sulfate for severe preeclampsia has a respiratory rate of 10/min, absent patellar reflexes, and urine output of 20 mL/hr. Identify the three immediate nursing actions.
items.content: Stop the magnesium sulfate infusion; notify the provider and activate urgent clinical response; prepare to administer prescribed calcium gluconate.
items.rationale: Respiratory depression, loss of reflexes, and oliguria suggest magnesium toxicity and reduced clearance. Stop the infusion, escalate immediately, support breathing, and prepare the antidote.

items.title: For each condition, identify the most appropriate additional precaution.
items.content: Pulmonary tuberculosis — Airborne; Clostridioides difficile infection — Contact; Influenza — Droplet; Disseminated herpes zoster — Airborne and Contact.
items.rationale: Precautions are selected by transmission route. C. difficile requires soap-and-water hand hygiene because spores resist alcohol-based sanitizer; disseminated zoster requires airborne and contact precautions.

items.title: Fifteen minutes after a packed RBC transfusion begins, the client develops chills, flank pain, and fever. The nurse should first ___ the transfusion and then maintain IV access with ___ using new tubing.
items.content: stop|normal saline
items.rationale: Stop the transfusion immediately for a suspected acute reaction. Keep the vein open with normal saline through new tubing, assess the client, notify the provider and blood bank, and follow facility protocol.

items.title: A client develops facial droop, dysarthria, and left-sided weakness 40 minutes ago. Glucose is 112 mg/dL and BP is 178/96 mm Hg. Complete the bowtie: identify the likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute stroke, likely ischemic|actions:activate stroke response and establish last-known-well time; arrange urgent noncontrast head CT and keep the client NPO until swallow screening|monitor:neurologic status using a standardized stroke scale; blood pressure and oxygenation
items.rationale: Time-sensitive stroke evaluation requires rapid activation, accurate last-known-well time, and urgent imaging to distinguish ischemia from hemorrhage. Avoid oral intake until swallowing is assessed to reduce aspiration risk.

items.title: Review the assessment note and identify the findings that indicate severe dehydration requiring urgent escalation.
items.content: An 8-month-old has had vomiting and diarrhea for 2 days. The infant is lethargic, has sunken eyes, a very dry mouth, capillary refill of 5 seconds, weak peripheral pulses, and no wet diaper for 10 hours. Temperature is 37.8°C.
items.rationale: Lethargy, markedly delayed capillary refill, weak pulses, and prolonged absence of urine indicate poor perfusion and severe fluid deficit. Sunken eyes and dry mucosa support dehydration.

items.title: The prescription is heparin 18 units/kg/hr for a client weighing 72 kg. The IV bag contains 25,000 units in 500 mL. How many mL/hr should the nurse program? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.content: 25.9 mL/hr
items.rationale: 18 units/kg/hr × 72 kg = 1,296 units/hr. The concentration is 25,000 units ÷ 500 mL = 50 units/mL. 1,296 ÷ 50 = 25.92 mL/hr, rounded to 25.9 mL/hr. Verify the calculation and infusion with the required independent double-check policy.

items.title: A client admitted with pneumonia has the following trend: 0800 RR 22/min, SpO₂ 94% on 2 L/min, alert; 1000 RR 30/min, SpO₂ 90% on 4 L/min, restless; 1200 RR 34/min, SpO₂ 86% on 6 L/min, drowsy. What is the priority interpretation and response?
items.content: The client is deteriorating with worsening hypoxemic respiratory failure; call rapid response/emergency support and prepare for advanced airway and ventilatory support.
items.rationale: Increasing oxygen requirement with falling saturation, tachypnea, and declining mental status indicates progressive respiratory failure. Escalate immediately rather than simply increasing oxygen without reassessment.

items.title: A 19-year-old with type 1 diabetes presents with vomiting, abdominal pain, deep rapid respirations, and fruity breath. Glucose is 486 mg/dL, pH 7.18, bicarbonate 10 mEq/L, potassium 5.4 mEq/L, and serum ketones are positive. Which initial intervention is the priority?
items.content: Begin prescribed isotonic IV fluid replacement and initiate close cardiac and electrolyte monitoring while preparing for IV insulin after potassium is assessed.
items.rationale: DKA causes profound dehydration and acidosis. Initial isotonic fluid resuscitation is essential. Serum potassium may be elevated despite total-body depletion; insulin shifts potassium intracellularly, so potassium must be monitored and managed safely.

items.title: On postoperative day 2 after hip replacement, a client suddenly develops dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, HR 132/min, and SpO₂ 84%. Which nursing actions should be taken immediately? Select all that apply.
items.content: Activate rapid response/emergency support; apply oxygen and support ventilation; keep the client on bed rest and avoid ambulation; maintain IV access and prepare for diagnostic evaluation and prescribed anticoagulation; continuously monitor oxygenation and hemodynamic status.
items.rationale: Sudden hypoxemia, tachycardia, and pleuritic pain after orthopedic surgery suggest pulmonary embolism. Stabilize airway and breathing, escalate care, limit exertion, and prepare for urgent evaluation and treatment.

items.title: Arrange the nursing actions in the appropriate sequence for a client with heavy postpartum bleeding and a boggy uterus.
items.content: 1. Call for assistance and initiate the postpartum hemorrhage response; 2. Massage the uterine fundus and assess uterine tone; 3. Administer prescribed oxytocin and other uterotonics as indicated; 4. Establish/maintain large-bore IV access, quantify blood loss, and prepare fluids/blood products; 5. Reassess vital signs, uterine tone, and bleeding continuously.
items.rationale: A boggy uterus suggests uterine atony. Immediate help and fundal massage are followed by uterotonic therapy and simultaneous resuscitation/preparation for blood products. Continue frequent reassessment and escalate if bleeding persists.

items.title: For each electrolyte imbalance, select all manifestations that are consistent with the condition.
items.content: Hyperkalemia — peaked T waves; muscle weakness; potentially widened QRS. Hypokalemia — U waves; muscle weakness; constipation. Hyponatremia — confusion; headache; seizures when severe. Hypercalcemia — constipation; polyuria; shortened QT interval.
items.rationale: Potassium abnormalities alter cardiac conduction and muscle function. Severe hyponatremia causes cerebral edema and neurologic symptoms. Hypercalcemia commonly causes gastrointestinal slowing, polyuria, and a shortened QT interval.

items.title: A hospitalized client says, “I have been thinking about ending my life, and I know exactly how I would do it.” What should the nurse do first?
items.content: Remain with the client, initiate immediate safety precautions, and obtain urgent assessment of plan, means, and intent according to protocol.
items.rationale: A specific plan indicates high acute risk. Do not leave the client alone; secure the environment and initiate urgent safety evaluation. A promise or no-suicide contract is not a substitute for safety measures.

items.title: The nurse is teaching a client newly prescribed warfarin for atrial fibrillation. Which statements indicate correct understanding? Select all that apply.
items.content: I will have my INR checked as scheduled; I will keep my intake of vitamin K-containing foods consistent; I will contact my provider before starting OTC medicines or supplements; I will seek urgent care for black stools or uncontrolled bleeding.
items.rationale: Warfarin requires INR monitoring and consistent vitamin K intake. Many medications and supplements interact with warfarin. Melena and uncontrolled bleeding may indicate serious hemorrhage.

items.title: A 4-year-old arrives drooling, sitting upright, febrile, and leaning forward with inspiratory stridor. Select the three priority nursing actions.
items.content: Keep the child calm and in the position of comfort; summon expert airway support and prepare for controlled airway management; avoid inspecting the throat or using a tongue blade.
items.rationale: Suspected epiglottitis can progress to complete airway obstruction. Agitation and throat examination may precipitate obstruction. Maintain a calm environment and prepare for expert airway intervention.

items.title: Match each medication with the adverse effect requiring priority monitoring.
items.content: Lisinopril — angioedema; Furosemide — hypokalemia; Gentamicin — nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity; Metformin — lactic acidosis in susceptible clinical situations.
items.rationale: ACE inhibitors can cause life-threatening angioedema. Loop diuretics can lower potassium. Aminoglycosides can damage kidneys and hearing. Metformin-associated lactic acidosis is rare but serious, particularly with significant renal impairment or hypoxia.

items.title: A client with a traumatic brain injury develops a widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, and irregular respirations. This pattern is called ___ and suggests ___ intracranial pressure.
items.content: Cushing triad|increased
items.rationale: Cushing triad is a late sign of increased intracranial pressure and possible impending herniation. It requires immediate escalation and interventions to prevent further increases in ICP.

items.title: Minutes after receiving an antibiotic, a client develops generalized urticaria, wheezing, facial swelling, and BP 76/40 mm Hg. Complete the bowtie.
items.content: condition:anaphylaxis with shock|actions:administer IM epinephrine promptly per emergency protocol; support airway and oxygenation and activate emergency response|monitor:airway patency and respiratory effort; blood pressure and perfusion
items.rationale: Anaphylaxis is a life-threatening airway and circulatory emergency. IM epinephrine is first-line treatment; antihistamines are adjuncts and must not delay epinephrine. Monitor for recurrent or biphasic symptoms.

items.title: Identify the assessment findings that indicate severe features and require urgent escalation.
items.content: At 34 weeks' gestation, a client has BP 168/112 mm Hg on repeat measurement, persistent severe headache, blurred vision, and right upper-quadrant pain. Platelets are 92,000/mm³ and AST is elevated.
items.rationale: Severe-range blood pressure, neurologic symptoms, epigastric/right upper-quadrant pain, thrombocytopenia, and elevated liver enzymes indicate severe disease and risk of maternal complications, including seizure and HELLP syndrome.

items.title: A child weighs 18 kg. The prescription is amoxicillin 45 mg/kg/day divided equally every 12 hours. The suspension is 400 mg/5 mL. How many mL should be given per dose? Round to the nearest tenth.
items.content: 5.1 mL
items.rationale: Daily dose = 45 mg/kg × 18 kg = 810 mg/day. Two doses per day = 405 mg/dose. Concentration = 400 mg/5 mL = 80 mg/mL. Volume = 405 ÷ 80 = 5.06 mL, rounded to 5.1 mL. Confirm the prescription, maximum dose, and product concentration before administration.

items.title: A client admitted with dehydration has the following trend: creatinine 1.0 to 2.1 to 3.0 mg/dL over 24 hours; urine output 45 to 20 to 10 mL/hr; potassium 4.2 to 5.1 to 6.0 mEq/L. What is the priority nursing response?
items.content: Escalate immediately for worsening acute kidney injury with oliguria and dangerous hyperkalemia; obtain/maintain cardiac monitoring and prepare for prescribed hyperkalemia treatment and renal evaluation.
items.rationale: Rising creatinine, falling urine output, and potassium 6.0 mEq/L indicate worsening renal function with risk of fatal dysrhythmia. Prompt escalation, ECG monitoring, and potassium-lowering treatment are required.

items.title: A 46-year-old with a history of gallstones reports severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and repeated vomiting. Lipase is markedly elevated. HR is 118/min, BP 94/58 mm Hg, and urine output is 20 mL/hr. Which finding is the strongest indication of a developing complication requiring urgent escalation?
items.content: Hypotension with oliguria and tachycardia, indicating intravascular volume depletion and impaired organ perfusion.
items.rationale: Acute pancreatitis can cause major third spacing and systemic inflammation. Hemodynamic instability and oliguria indicate compromised perfusion and possible severe disease; prioritize resuscitation and close monitoring.

items.title: Which nursing practices reduce the risk of central line-associated bloodstream infection? Select all that apply.
items.content: Perform hand hygiene before line access; disinfect the connector for the required friction and drying time; use aseptic technique for dressing changes; assess daily whether the line remains necessary; remove the catheter promptly when no longer indicated.
items.rationale: Hand hygiene, connector disinfection, aseptic dressing care, and daily necessity review reduce contamination and line exposure. Follow the device-specific antisepsis and dressing-change protocol.

items.title: Place the nursing actions in priority order for a client with severe asthma, audible wheezing, accessory muscle use, and SpO₂ 88%.
items.content: 1. Rapidly assess airway, breathing, speech, and oxygenation while calling for urgent assistance; 2. Administer prescribed oxygen and rapid-acting inhaled bronchodilator; 3. Administer prescribed systemic corticosteroid and additional adjunct therapy as indicated; 4. Reassess work of breathing, breath sounds, oxygenation, and response; 5. Escalate immediately for exhaustion, altered mental status, or a silent chest.
items.rationale: Initial management supports oxygenation and rapidly reverses bronchospasm. Corticosteroids reduce airway inflammation but have delayed onset. A silent chest or declining consciousness signals impending respiratory failure.

items.title: For each burn-related finding, identify the appropriate nursing interpretation or response.
items.content: Hoarseness and soot around the mouth after an enclosed-space fire — suspect inhalation injury and prepare for early airway management. Circumferential chest burn with reduced chest expansion — urgent evaluation for restrictive eschar. Decreasing urine output during resuscitation — reassess perfusion and prescribed fluid titration. New confusion with hypotension — suspect inadequate perfusion and escalate.
items.rationale: Airway edema can progress rapidly after inhalation injury. Circumferential full-thickness burns may restrict ventilation or circulation. Urine output and mental status are important perfusion indicators during burn resuscitation.

items.title: A client with a chest tube for pneumothorax accidentally disconnects the drainage tubing from the collection system. What should the nurse do immediately?
items.content: Place the end of the chest tube in sterile water to re-establish a temporary water seal, then reconnect to a new drainage system per protocol.
items.rationale: A temporary sterile-water seal helps prevent air from entering the pleural space while the system is replaced. Assess respiratory status and obtain assistance; do not clamp the tube routinely because tension pneumothorax can develop.

items.title: A client experiencing acute mania is pacing, speaking rapidly, and has eaten very little. Which nursing interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Provide a low-stimulation environment; offer high-calorie finger foods and fluids; use brief, clear directions and consistent limits; reduce competitive group activities; monitor sleep, hydration, and exhaustion.
items.rationale: Mania increases activity and distractibility while reducing attention to nutrition and rest. Low stimulation, portable nutrient-dense foods, clear limits, and monitoring support safety and basic needs.

items.title: A client with a tibial fracture in a cast reports escalating pain despite opioids. The affected foot is pale and paresthetic, and passive toe extension causes severe pain. Select the three priority actions.
items.content: Notify the orthopedic surgeon/emergency team immediately; prepare for urgent pressure-relieving intervention such as fasciotomy; perform and document frequent neurovascular assessments without delaying escalation.
items.rationale: Pain out of proportion and pain with passive stretch are early warning signs of compartment syndrome. Pulses may remain present until late. This is a limb-threatening emergency requiring immediate surgical evaluation.

items.title: Match each fetal heart rate pattern with its most likely cause.
items.content: Early decelerations — fetal head compression. Variable decelerations — umbilical cord compression. Late decelerations — uteroplacental insufficiency. Sinusoidal pattern — possible severe fetal anemia or hypoxia.
items.rationale: Early decelerations mirror contractions and are usually benign. Variable decelerations are abrupt and associated with cord compression. Late decelerations begin after the contraction starts and suggest impaired uteroplacental perfusion.
